title: Rotokakahi A3B1B1B — list of owners as at 14 Aug 1940 (Matiu Wiripo and three Rihari Matiu children) with schedule of ownership orders 1969–1990
summary: Nine pages (area 57:3:36 = 23.4363 ha; 63.636 shares). The 1940 list has just four owners: MATIU WIRIPO 36.363 (4/7) and Rirena Arama @ Rirena Rihari Matiu, "Tame Rihari Matiu @ Manuera Rihari Matiu" and Whina Rihari Matiu, 9.091 each (1/7) — the block came down through Matiu Wiripo, with Rihari Matiu's three children already holding their father's share. Then: (a) 4 Nov 1969 Rirena vested her 9.091 in her sons Makura (4.546) and Charlie Arama (4.545); (b) 3 Mar 1970 Matiu Wiripo's 36.363 was divided among his lines (S.V.O., KT 6/32-13): Wiremu Matiu and Reta Waipouri (2.577 each), the seven "Te Okena Matiu" children (Topia, Takuira, Pataraki or Pataraki Atama, Manuera, Iwa, Mane…), Te Okena and Hone Piriparaihe (Ruhia's line), the four Rihari Matiu children Rirena, Rata, Hira and HARE (1.299 each), the Maihi/Rurawhe line, the Wikitaringi Taitimu line, the Hapakuku, Wharewaka and Wi Hone lines; (c) 9 Nov 1970 WHINA's 9.091 went solely to "Rirena Rihari Matiu or Rirena Arama of Pawarenga" (KT 6/315); (d) 20 Oct 1981 Rirena's 10.390 to her EIGHT children — Lucy Nicholas, Michael, Makura, Graham, Andrew, Ken Arama, Hannah Wano and Charlie Arama, 1.299 each; (e) 1990 Makura's share to Michael Arama and Charlie's to Hannah Wano. Also Arapeta Peri Paraihe (list 15, 1.731) to the Public Trustee, 1982. The 1970 succession is the Court's own statement that the Te Okena (Atama) Matiu children, Ruhia's Piriparaihe sons and Rihari Matiu's children were all Matiu Wiripo's descendants.

title: Rotokakahi A — succession register 1889–1896: Wiremu Paraihe and Mereana Paraihe to Peri Paraihe, Hira Amuketi and Mereana Pirini (16 Mar 1896)
summary: Four register pages for the parent block Rotokakahi A, successions 1889–1896. Page 3 carries the earliest Paraihe record in this collection: WIREMU PARAIHE (d. 19 Dec 1891) and MEREANA PARAIHE, each succeeded on 16 March 1896 by Peri Paraihe (m), Hira Amuketi (f) and Mereana Pirini (f), one third each — the same three who took Hone Paraihe's Whakakoro F4 interest in 1914 (Hira by then dead and represented by her Amuketi children). This confirms Hira Amuketi as Peri Paraihe's sister and adds two more Paraihe (Wiremu and Mereana) who died before 1896 and whose relationship — sibling or parent — the register does not state. Also the Tipene (Hone Tana Papahia), Rikihana, Paraone, Hokopu and other families of Rotokakahi A.

title: Rotokakahi A3B1B1B — succession order schedule: Peri Paraihe (1936), Ria Hone Wharewaka (1940) and the exchange orders of 14 Aug 1940 consolidating Peri Paraihe's interest in Rirena, Tame and Whina Rihari Matiu
summary: Form 16 schedule for Rotokakahi A3B1B1B. (1) Peri Paraihe alias Kaperiere Paraihe (d. 1929): the same nine-way succession of 25 Sep 1936 as in Whakakoro F4 and Oturu A, with Rirena Arama trustee for Whina and Ria Hone Wharewaka trustee for the Okena Peri children. (2) Ria Hone Wharewaka (d. by 1940): her fifth to Wati Ratahi Topia, Erina, Rauriti, Ani and Ihaka Hone Wharewaka. (3) Two EXCHANGE ORDERS of 14 Aug 1940 (HK 17/294-5 and 296-7) by which Arapeta and Hone Peri Paraihe, the three Okena Peri children and Ria's five successors all gave up their Rotokakahi A3B1B1B shares to Rirena, Tame (Manuera) and Whina Rihari Matiu — so that by the 14 Aug 1940 list (doc 1279339) Rihari Matiu's three children held the whole of Peri Paraihe's 3/7 of the block (9.091 each) beside Matiu Wiripo's 4/7. This is the mechanism by which the Rihari Matiu line consolidated Peri Paraihe's Rotokakahi interest — and, presumably, gave up shares elsewhere in return.

title: Auckland minute book 11 AT 300 — sitting of 17 November 1980: Rirena Arama (s 78A) — Erihapeti Arama 'also known as Betty' sworn as applicant and daughter; nine children listed; will not produced (item 60, continues on 301)
blocks_recorded: (minute book page — Rirena Arama's estate; her interests were in Rotokakahi A3B1B1B, Paihia 1D1E2, Owhata C and the Peri Paraihe blocks)
court: Māori Land Court, Tai Tokerau (sitting at Auckland)
summary: One handwritten page, folio 300 of Auckland minute book 11 (book scan 01076422), margin date 17.11.80. (a) Tail of an earlier, unrelated item: '… and transfer to person entitled. Please return probate to Mrs Thorne(?) with form. Fee on application is remitted and to be applied to Registrar's application for vesting.' (b) Item 60: 'RIRENA ARAMA (S. 78A). Erihapeti Arama: Applicant. Sworn: Also known as Betty. My mother died on the 26th April 1980 at Pa[wa]renga. I was present at her tangi. She left a will. Court: Who are present in Court. Present: 1. Lucy Nicholas f.a. [Māngere]; 2. Betty or Erihapeti Hori f.a. [c/- Mauku, R.D. 3 Pukekohe]; 3. [a first name struck through, "Michael" written above] Michael Arama m.a. c/- No 1 above; 4. Makura Arama m.a. [Manurewa]; 5. Graham Arama m.a. [Māngere]; 6. Andrew Arama m.a. c/- No 4; 7. Ken Arama m.a. [Papakura]; 8. Hannah Wano f.a. c/- P.O. Ōpononi [margin: Absent]; 9. Charlie Arama m.a. c/- No 1. Court: The will has not been produced, only an unsigned copy. The solicitor has will. Registrar to write and ask for its production. Family are to discuss with Mr Noa[—]' — the sentence runs on to folio 301. Street addresses are in the minute but are not reproduced here. Significance: Betty/Erihapeti Hori swears that Rirena was her mother, and the Court lists her as one of nine children present or accounted for — the same sibling set that took Rirena's Paihia, Rotokakahi and Owhata interests on 20 Oct 1981 (AT 12/360), minus Betty. The will was still outstanding on 1 Jul 1981 (12 AT 232, item 62: solicitor Malcolm Douglas, Manurewa).

(a) The upper two-thirds belong to another family's matter: 'Order: s 136 as follows — Panguru B30 5, value $245, to Nos 1–4 above 1/9th share each, No 11 1/9th solely, Nos 12–18 1/63rd, Nos 19–21 1/27th, Nos 24–28 1/45th, Nos 32–34 and 37–42 1/81st. The above block has potential afforestation value. Wharau 5 to Adelaide Wood(?), No … above, solely. Rebecca's children were present when all agreed that only one person be put in to this small interest and that as the youngest surviving daughter it should go to Adelaide.' A later note in another hand — '(Refer to AT 16/219-220 for final [orders])' — sits between the two items and most probably belongs to that matter. (b) '60 (cont'd) RIRENA ARAMA, S. 78A. See folio 300/301. Court: The titles officer has discussed an arrangement with the family. The Court awaits production of original will but is prepared to make provisional orders subject to ratification by Judge in Chambers when original will to hand.' The page ends there; the provisional orders themselves should follow on folio 354. Read with 11 AT 300 (17 Nov 1980: Erihapeti/Betty applicant, nine children listed), 12 AT 232 (1 Jul 1981: will still outstanding; Wiremu Arama's interests vested in Betty alone) and the final order AT 12/360 (20 Oct 1981, 'in terms of will', to the other eight), this is the Court's own record that the 1981 outcome was a negotiated family arrangement.

title: Auckland minute book 11 AT 354 — 20 November 1980: the whānau arrangement on Rirena Arama's estate — Erihapeti (Betty) to take nothing from her mother and her father's land interests solely; s 78A orders to the other eight
court: Māori Land Court, Tai Tokerau (sitting at Auckland)
summary: Folio 354 of Auckland minute book 11 (book scan 01076422), 20.11.80, continuing item 60 from folio 353. Verbatim: 'There were 8 of the 9 children entitled under the will present in Court and these children met with Mr Naera, Titles Officer, to discuss an arrangement. They were unanimous and it was decided that Erihapeti — No 2 on folio 300 — would not take any interest from her mother but she would take her father's land interests solely when succession was put through. Accordingly the Court determines that persons entitled are Nos 1–9 on folio 300. Orders Section 78A as follows: Rotokakahi A3B1B1B $680, Owhata C $376, Te Puna-o-Hokianga $34 — to Nos 1, 3–9 inclusive a 1/8th share each; Paihia 1D1E1 $14, Paihia 1M5 $7 — to No 3 solely; Paihia 1D1E2 $79 — Nos 1, 8, 9 & 4 a 1/4th share equally; Paihia 1D1L $25, Paihia 1D1M $39 — Nos 5, 6, 7 a 1/3rd share equally. The Deputy Registrar will please forward a copy of these minutes to applicant.' (Nos refer to the list on folio 300: 1 Lucy Nicholas, 2 Betty/Erihapeti Hori, 3 Michael Arama, 4 Makura Arama, 5 Graham Arama, 6 Andrew Arama, 7 Ken Arama, 8 Hannah Wano, 9 Charlie Arama.) These are the provisional orders later sealed as AT 12/360 (20 Oct 1981, 'in terms of will', doc 1355796) after the original will was produced; the other half of the arrangement is the s 136 order of 1 Jul 1981 vesting Wiremu Arama's interests in Betty solely (doc 1355755).

summary: Page 1: typed list of the 31 owners of Paihia 1D1E2 (area 19:2:27 = 7.9596 ha; 216.666 shares; file no. 9294), with later strike-throughs pointing to successor list numbers. Pages 2–6: handwritten schedule of ownership orders, entries 32–80 (1979–1995). Whānau entries: no. 25 "Rirena Rihari Matiu or Rirena Arana [Arama]" 5.317 → 20 Oct 1981 (AT 12/360) to Lucy Nicholas, Makura Arama, Hannah Wano and Charlie Arama equally — Rirena's successors, a year after her death; Makura (Makura Albert Cassidy Arama) → 1993 to Christine Anne Arama, Hannah Margaret Adams, Jason Arama. No. 6 "Hira Rihari Matui" 5.318 (still on title) and no. 23 "Rata Rihari Matui" 5.317 (→ 1994 to six successors) — two further Rihari Matiu children alongside Rirena, each with the same share. No. 2 "Arapeta Piriparaihe" = Arapeta Peri Paraihe or Albert Peri → 1982 via the Public Trustee to nine children (Henry, Richard, Frances, Wiremu, Annette, Alfred, Anthony, John Peri (Paraihe) and Jane Takurua). Nos 7 and 17, Hone and Te Okena Piriparaihe, 5.318 each, still standing unsucceeded. The six equal 5.317/5.318 shares (Arapeta, Hone, Te Okena; Hira, Rata, Rirena) total 31.905 — consistent with one earlier interest divided in two (Ruhia Matiu Wiripo's three sons; Rihari Matiu's three children), i.e. an interest that came down from Matiu Wiripo through both a daughter (Ruhia) and a son (Rihari). The Atama/Manihera owners are the Atama Matiu line (Wati Manihera absorbing five interests 1981–82).

title: Paihia 1D1E — schedule of ownership orders: successions to Pati Wharewaka (1940) and Atama Matiu (1952)
summary: One handwritten page of the "Schedule of Ownership Orders" for Paihia 1D1E (shares 216.666). Two successions: Pati Wharewaka (list no. 2, 20.000; S.O. 13.8.40) to Mane, Takuira, Topia, Paterihi, Manuera and Iwa Atama (1/7 each) and to Pita, Takuira, Ihipeti, Nikora, Wati and Katarina Manihera (1/42 each); and Atama Matiu (list no. 1, 85.000; S.O. 28.3.52) to Toma Atama (3/17) and the same six Atama children (2/17 each) and six Manihera grandchildren (1/51 each). The Paihia 1D title came through Matiu Wiripo (succession from Pirini Wiripo, 1910 — doc 1445102), so "Atama Matiu" is very probably a son of Matiu Wiripo, i.e. a brother of Rihari Matiu, and Pati Wharewaka his wife — a Matiu–Wharewaka marriage in the same generation as Ria Hone Wharewaka (Peri Paraihe's daughter, whose "Hone Wharewaka" is presumably a married name). "Topia" (Topia Atama) is the name that later appears as Wati Ratahi Topia and Erina Rutuki Topia, successors to Ria Hone Wharewaka in Whakakoro F4.

title: Paihia 1D1C — succession order schedule 1929–1950 (7 pages): Ruhia Peri Matiu and the Peri Matiu children
summary: Seven pages of Form 16 succession order schedules for Paihia 1D1C. Key whānau entries (p.1, all 3 July 1929, HK 10/94): three children who died young — "Roi Matiu" (1906), "Hoana Peri Matiu" (1907) and "Hana Peri Matiu" (1909) — succeeded by "Ruhia Peri Matiu, f.a." solely (Hana's half shared with Iri Tamaho Maika). This is Ruhia Matiu Wiripo, Peri Paraihe's second wife, recorded under her married form "Ruhia Peri Matiu", with a small annotation of a further name (Horomona / Paura Taitimu). In 1940 she took 1/8 of Parani Ritete alias Parani Rewi (d. 1916) alongside Iri Tamaho Maika (1/8) — an unexplained close tie to the Ritete/Rewi whānau — and her and Iri's interests were the subject of an exchange order (HK 17/315, 16.8.40). Page 5 repeats the Pati Wharewaka succession of 13.8.40 with her full name "Pati Wharewaka Topia" and Atama Matiu as trustee. Other Paihia 1D1C families: Ritete/Pirini/Tahana, Ihaka Uruhau, Hira Tukino, Herehana, Taitimu Tahana, Angel, Karaweia/Rameka/Matiu Kapa.

title: Waihapa — succession register 1880–1910: Hare Hongi Hika to Rongo Kahira, Mereana Paora, Tura Wiremu and five others (27 Feb 1890)
summary: Three pages of the Waihapa succession register (two handwritten register pages and a Form 16 schedule). Page 2: HARE HONGI HIKA, succession order 27 February 1890 (N4/119) to Rongo Kahira (m), Mereana Paora (f), TURA WIREMU (f), Rati Pona (m), Wini Tuta (m), Huia Miriama (f), Arihia Hemi (f) and Poni Rewharewha (f). This is the clearest Court record of Tura — "Tura Hongi" on the 1876 memorial, "Tura Wiremu" here after her marriage to Wiremu Tangata — succeeding to her father, and it fixes the membership of the Hāre Hongi Hika descent group that reappears as group A in the 1895 Pokaka title. Other entries: Ruinga Tapu (1880), Te Arama / Hone Kingi Tapu (1885), Hori Kerei, the Toetoe family (1890), Aporo te Meawai, Wakahe alias Te Hie, Meta Tapu, Erana Raupane alias Erana Ururoa (to the Snowden children, 1894), Mio Tuauru (1910).

title: Taupo 23C — succession order schedule: Taniora Rihari or Rihari Taniora (d. 1922), order 29 Feb 1932; Matire Taniora (d. 1918); Manga Taniora Rihari (1962)
summary: Two-page Form 16 succession order schedule for Taupo 23C. Page 2 is the key whānau record: "Taniora Rihari or Rihari Taniora", died 1922 (N66A/99), succession order 29 February 1932 dividing his interest into SEVENTHS — (1) Manga Taniora Rihari m, (2) Rihari Taniora Rihari m, (3) the seven children of the late Hetaraka Taniora at 1/49 each (Maki, Hoana, Pera, Te Hape or Hone, Te Kui or Marara, Himi, Pueti; trustee Rahera Hetaraka Taniora), (4) the EIGHT children of the late Arama Taniora at 1/56 each — Mane, Peepi, WIREMU, Arama or Honetiaki II, Raiha, Taitimu, Mio and Rirena Arama Taniora — with "Tr: PETI WIREMU TANGATA" (their mother Erihapeti, Arama Taniora's widow), (5) Werahiko and Te Uinga Pereene Kini, Maori Moana Tarapatiki and Peka Toma Ngarangi at 1/28, (6) Mita and Tupakongia Heremaia Kingi at 1/14 (trustee Peti Kingi), (7) the four Hamuera Herewini children at 1/28 — who also took, 1/4 each, the interest of Matire Taniora (d. 1918, N66A/102), evidently their mother and Taniora Rihari's daughter. Years written beside the minors (1924–1943) are coming-of-age years. A 1962 succession vesting order (N 86/126) passes Manga Taniora Rihari's share solely to Maria Maudy Rihari. Page 1: Maata Putete Hape (d. 1933) to eight Hare Paora/Hongi successors (1938); Matarae Arano (d. 31.12.32) to Mere Matarae Arano (1951). This one page gives Taniora Rihari's seven lines of descent and names all eight of Arama Taniora and Peti's children — including a second "Rirena" (Rirena Arama Taniora, b. c. 1912, Wiremu Arama's sister), distinct from Rirena Theresa Arama née Rihari Matiu (b. c. 1911), Wiremu's wife.

title: Taupo 23C — compiled list of owners as at 28 Aug 1957 (38 owners, 36.000 shares) with schedule of ownership orders 1932–1957
summary: Four pages: (1) typed "Compiled List of Owners as at 28/8/57" for Taupo 23C (38:0:20; 36.000 shares), 38 owners; (2–4) the typed schedule of ownership orders, entries 9–56. The original owners (list nos 1–8) included ARAMA TANIORA (no. 1, 5.000 shares — N66A/100), "HIMI TANIORA RIHARI" (no. 2, 4.000 — N66A/99, i.e. Taniora Rihari under a third recorded name), Matarae Arano (5, 5.000), Matire Taniora (6, 4.000), Maata Putete Hape (7, 6.000) and Rihari Taniora Rihari (8, 4.000). On 29 Feb 1932 Taniora Rihari's 4.000 went in sevenths (nos 9–35) and Arama Taniora's own 5.000 went equally to his eight children (nos 49–56, 0.625 each), so that Mane, Peepi, Wiremu, Arama or Honetiaki II, Raiha, Taitimu, Mio and Rirena Arama Taniora each held 0.696 by 1957 — the figure still carried by the six survivors on the 2009 list, with Betty Arama/Hori holding Wiremu's. Rihari Taniora Rihari: 4.000 + 0.571 = 4.571 (as in 2009).

title: Auckland minute book 12 AT 232 — sitting of 1 July 1981: Rirena Rihari Matiu (Mrs Arama), succession held up pending her will (item 62); Wiremu Arama Taniora dec'd, Erihapeti Arama sworn as applicant and daughter (item 72, continues on 233)
blocks_recorded: (minute book page — Wiremu Arama Taniora and Rirena Rihari Matiu successions; the 1 Jul 1981 order covered Taupo 23C, Tauaki, Mangaiti 3B, Waihapa 2B4B and Otangaroa 1C3B1)
court: Māori Land Court, Tai Tokerau (sitting at Auckland)
summary: One handwritten page, folio 232 of Auckland minute book 12 (Pātaka Whenua page 233 of book scan 01076095), headed 'Auckland … 1.7.81'. Three items. (a) Tail of an earlier application about a lease fixture: 'with the consent of the lessee, the Maori Land Board, the Commissioner of Crown Lands. Court: Discussed matter with parties. The application is adjourned to a fixture to be arranged by the applicant or his solicitor after consultation with the Board, Mr [Moanan?] or his solicitor and the Court Registrar. Adjourned in interim to next Whangarei [sitting] but may be later adjourned if negotiations still proceeding.' Copies to the Maori Land Board, Mr [Moanan?] and Mr [Rahiti?] of [Pegg Bros?] — not whānau business. (b) Item 62, '3 copies 1.7.81': 'RIRENA RIHARI MATIU (Mrs ARAMA) (S 78A/67). Court: I refer to AT 11/300-301. Acting Registrar is to write to Malcolm Douglas, Solicitor, Manurewa and request him to forward original will to Court so that succession can be completed. File to be referred to Court for order when will received.' — i.e. Rirena (T901, d. 1980) left a will held by a Manurewa solicitor, and her succession (made 20 Oct 1981, AT 12/360) waited on it. (c) Item 72, '3 copies 1.7.81': 'WIREMU ARAMA TANIORA Dec'd (S 135). Erihapeti Arama sworn: I am the applicant. The deceased was my father. Died at Pawarenga on the 4th June 1966. I was' — the evidence continues on folio 233 (not in this file). This is the minute behind the 1 Jul 1981 sole succession of 'Betty or Erihapeti Arama or Hori' to Wiremu Arama's interests (order 136/53) in Taupo 23C, Tauaki, Mangaiti 3B, Waihapa 2B4B and Otangaroa 1C3B1.

judge: T K T A R Williams
summary: Court minute (pānui) of the hearing at Auckland on 8 October 2026 before Judge T K T A R Williams (T Hepi, clerk; B Ward, registrar; M Rapana, court assistant) on an application under ss 113 and 118 of Te Ture Whenua Māori Act 1993 to succeed to the Māori land interests of Wiremu Tangata, also known as Wiremu Tangiwhare and Wiremu Tana. Facts found: died 13 February 1927 at Ōmaunu (death certificate); born c. 1861; child of Ani Tangiwhare and Tangiwhare; no will and no assets requiring a grant of administration; no partner at death; three children — Mate Wiremu Tangata (f, other parent Tura Wiremu Tangata; predeceased, leaving Toetoe Whitinui m and Mereana Whitinui f), Ani Wiremu Tangata (f, d. 15 March 1927) and Erihapeti also known as Betty Arama or Adams or Peti Wiremu Tangata (f, d. 18 March 1960). Interests: Pokaka B2B (LINZ 504121, current owner 'Wiremu Tangiwhare', 1 share) and Te Pupuke Church Site & Tapu (LINZ 509887, 'Wiremu Tangata', 1 share). Orders: s 113 — persons entitled 1/3 Ani Wiremu Tangata, 1/3 Erihapeti aka Betty Arama aka Adams, 1/6 each Toetoe Whitinui and Mereana Whitinui; s 118 — interests vested accordingly; order to be completed without delay under r 7.5(2)(b) of the Māori Land Court Rules 2011; copy of the minute to all parties. The Court noted that Ani and Erihapeti died after Wiremu Tangata and that separate succession applications are required for their estates, fee waived if filed within 12 months. The division matches the Te Pupuke J succession of 20 July 1949 (N 27/397). Date-of-death note: the 1949 schedule recorded 31 Dec 1925; the death certificate filed in 2025 gives 13 Feb 1927.

title: Whakakoro F / F Sec 4 — succession order schedule and schedule of ownership orders, 1910–1960 (13 pages)
summary: The Court's running record of successions for Whakakoro F (p.1) and Whakakoro F Sec 4 (pp.2–13): handwritten Form 16 succession order schedules (pp.1–5) followed by the numbered "Schedule of Ownership Orders" (pp.6–13, list numbers 20–137, base 1286.666 shares). It carries the whānau line through four generations on one title: HONE PARAIHE (d. before 1914) → 28.4.14: PERI PARAIHE 1/3 (32.667), Mereana Pirini 1/3, four Amuketi grandchildren 1/12 each → PERI PARAIHE alias Kaperiere Paraihe (HK 15/261, 25.9.36): Rirena Arama, Tame and Whina Rihari Matiu 2.178 each (Rirena trustee for Whina), Ria Hone Wharewaka 6.533, Hone Peri Paraihe 6.533, Rawiri/Ngarimu/Hone Okena Peri 2.178 each (Ria trustee), Arapeta Peri Paraihe 6.533 → Ria Hone Wharewaka d. by 13.8.40: five successors (Topia / Hone Wharewaka) → Hone Peri Paraihe d. 16.12.50: Robert James Perry sole (13.3.57) → Rawiri, Ngarimu and Hone Okena Peri d. by 1959: Arapeta sole (21.10.59), 13.067 as "Albert Peri @ Arapeta Peri Paraihe". Rirena's 2.178 (1936) had become 6.534 by c. 1988 — exactly three 2.178 shares, consistent with her succeeding to Tame and Whina (not recorded in this schedule, which ends 1960). Also: Queenie Matiu sole successor to Kahutahua Timoti Puhipi (22.000) 1.11.60; Maraea Pene (1910 successor to Piri Korotu) d. 27.9.30 → Pene Wiripo/Wiropo d. 1943 → seven Pene Wiropo children.

title: Minute book 15 HK 261 — succession to Peri Paraihe alias Kaperiere Paraihe, whakapapa read in Court (25 Sep 1936)
court: Native Land Court, Tokerau District, sitting at Pawarenga
judge: F. O. V. Acheson
summary: Hokianga minute book 15, folio 261, 25 September 1936. Applications 246–258 (plus Paihia 1M3A and Wairoa A) — succession to Peri Paraihe alias Kaperiere Paraihe in fifteen blocks. The Court read out the whakapapa supplied by Mr Tamaho McMath: 1st wife Horomena Toriwhina = Peri Paraihe = 2nd wife Ruhia Matiu Wiripo. By the 1st wife: Maraea (deceased) = Rihari Matiu, whose children are Rirena Arama (f.a.), Tame Rihari Matiu (m.a.) and Whina Rihari Matiu (f., 18); and Ria Hone Wharewaka (f.a.). By the 2nd wife: Hone Peri Paraihe (m.a.); Okena P.P. (deceased), whose children are Rawiri Okena Peri (m., 15), Ngarimu (f., 9) and Hone (m., 13); Pirini P.P. (deceased, no issue); Arapeta P.P. (m.a.). Written approval of the whakapapa and request that all share in proper proportion lodged by Ria, Hone, Arapeta, Rirena and Tame; all present except Hone (ill). A will dated 5/8/27 lodged by Tamaho McMath at Rawene 9/9/36 was far too late for probate and the Court would not have approved its contents; the family agreed it be taken no notice of. Deceased died 7 September 1929. Orders: succession orders accordingly in favour of all nine as above; trustee for Whina to be [name illegible]; trustee for Okena's children to be Ria.

title: Otangaroa No 1 — memorial of ownership register: owners and successions 1878–1894 (incl. Hare Hongi Hika, 1890)
summary: The Court's register page for Otangaroa No 1 (memorial of ownership vol. 1 fol. 64, 9 Oct 1876, 3439a 2r): the 17 owners, then "Deceased / Successors" 1878–1894. summary: Forty-six pages (hand-written MLC 102 / Form 16 schedules, then typed): (1) F. E. Maning's 1867 list of the 25 persons interested in Te Kohanga No. 1 under s.17 of the Native Lands Act 1867 — Mumu Ngapipi, Puhipi, Te Pana, Hamihana, Kingi Wiremu, Nepia, Honi Te Karaparapa, Timoti Puhipi, Te Waaka Rangaunu, Taipari (the ten named in the Crown grant), Poharama, Te Henare, Paora, Te Kirihini Nepia, Te Rapihana, Ranga, Takerei, Hamiora, Patana, Meri, Erina, Herepete, Wiremu Tana Hamihana, Hapita, Makoare Haki; (2) succession orders 1875–1909 (Kingi Wiremu, Te Pana, Takerei, Erina, the 1896 sitting — Meri → Raniera Matiu and Tamihana Rihimona; Makoare Haki; Herepete; Hamihana Paka; **Hamiora Rungaiterangi alias Hamiora → Rihipeti Arama, Hariata Haimona, Te Wikiriwhi Poutu, 5.9.1896** — Te Waaka Rangaunu, Honi te Karaparapa, Nepia, Patana te Maru (1901), Poharama Karanui (1905), Mumu Ngapipi and Taipari (1909)); (3) orders 1912–62 including Rihipeti Arama (d. 17.12.1922) → Eruera Paora (1925) → the Eruera Wahapu / Makinira Wiremu children (1944), the big Whangaroa/Kaitaia sitting of 18–19 Nov 1931 (N66A), Kiritiana Matiu → her Matiu children (1936, as on Karikari 2), the Hohipa, Mihaka, Nopera Arano and Natanahira lines and the 1949 exchange orders against Parengarenga 5B2B; (4) the typed schedule of ownership orders (nos 26–338); (5) the compiled list of 171 owners as at 6.3.1963 (25.000 shares). The 1965 Te Kohanga (Lots 1, 3–27) list of 329 owners / 1,745 shares (docs 1391494, 1391616) is a later, larger title.

notes: Attached to the chat 6 Oct 2026 (the Drive copy is 11 MB, over the connector limit). Answers D009: the Rihipeti Arama of Te Kohanga No. 1 succeeded in 1896 to HAMIORA (Rungaiterangi), not to a Himiona, and died 17 Dec 1922 — so she is not Erihapeti Arama née Wiremu Tangata (1880–1960). No Himiona, Tangata or Renata appears on Te Kohanga No. 1 at any date. The "Rihipeti Arama 24.405" on the 1965 Te Kohanga list is absent from the 1963 Te Kohanga 1 list, so it derives from another parent block of the 1965 title (Te Kohanga 2?), not from No. 1. Pages 1–41 read in full for the whānau questions; the 171-owner 1963 list is entered for nos 1–42 and selected others. D015 contradicted 17 Oct 2026 — Rihipeti Arama (d. 1922) is not Raiha Taniora (d. 1897).

title: Karikari No. 2 — succession, exchange and vesting order schedules 1916–1974, with the compiled list of owners as at 4 Nov 1960
summary: Twelve pages of Karikari No. 2 (760 acres, 325.397 shares) schedules: (pp.1–2) successions 1916–1939 — Karena, Wiremu and Amiria Tipene (1916), Ho Paihana (d. 1.6.20; s.o. 1921 → Hami Ho Paihana and Ho Berghan), Wiremu Hoani Tana (d. 29.12.19; nine children 1921), Matiu Paewoi (d. 26.7.10; s.o. 22.2.22 → Reihana, Waata, Wiremu, Tiini, Miriama, Toni Matiu), Merepaea Wiremu Karetana (1922 → seven Wiremu children), Miriama Matiu (1928 → Erana, Kare, Rina, Aue Umuroa), Kiritiana Matiu (list 28; 1936 → her children Raniera @ Waata, Miha, Reihana, Wiremu, Riwhi @ Tiini and Heni Matiu, and Miriama's children), Ruki Tipene (1939 → Miriama, Erina, Riria), Waata Matiu's 1937 gift to Karaitiana, Patana and Mei Raniera Matiu; (pp.3, 6–7) exchange orders 1949–51 consolidating the Wiremu Tana, Wiremu, Kakuere, Tipene and Rupapera interests in the Matiu, Motu and Marara Wiremu Taka lines; (pp.3–5) vesting orders 1957–61 — Heni Matiu @ Heni Hamuera Rupapera (d. 3.12.54 → Pawhau and Uporo Rupapera), Kare Tana, Hora Hemi (1961 order later cancelled), Nepia Rewi (1960 → six Nepia Rewe children), Aue Umuroa (1961 → Rangi Hiroa Fletcher for life, eight Fletcher children); (pp.8–9) compiled list of 41 owners as at 4.11.60; (pp.10–12) orders 1969–74 — Hora Hemi's 50.000 to eighteen (later Karikari 2B), Uporo Rupapera → Julia Matiu, Miha Matiu → six, Raniera @ Waata Matiu → his three children, Hami Ho Paihana → Agnes Anderson, Ho Berghan → Simon Matthew Urlich, Mahurangi Motu → Official Assignee → Agnes Anderson, Erana Umuroa → six Cross/Umuroa/Smith children.

title: Schedule of ownership orders — Karikari 2J (partition order 24 Jul 1979; Marara Wiremu Taka sole; 1984 transfer to eight)
summary: Karikari 2J, 26.3700 ha, 50.001 shares, created by partition order 24/7/1979. Sole owner Marara Wiremu Taka (f., deceased), Ngaire Morrison as administratrix of her estate. By order under s.81A/67 dated 30.5.84 (list 1, 50.001 shares) the estate (deceased/transferor "Ngaire Morrison as administratrix to the estate of Marara Wiremu Taka or Marara …") passed to eight: Ngaire Morrison 1/4, Miro Stevens 1/4, Hinumi Rikihana 1/4, and Carla, James, Athol and Harawira Raika 1/16 each. Entered 30/8/85. Karikari 2J is now three titles (2J1–2J3).

Largest interests: Simon Matthew Urlich 64.285, Phillip Mathews 59.202, Agnes Anderson 50.000, Marara Wiremu Taka 50.001, the three Raniera Matiu children 23.454–23.455 each, Julia Matiu and Pawhau Rupapera 13.293 each, Mori Nepia Reewe 12.500. title: Parengarenga 3G — schedule of ownership orders (19 pages): compiled list of 57 owners as at 7 Sep 1959 (55.000 shares, 511.8261 ha) and the orders of 1965–1997 (nos 58–386) — the Anaru/Anderson, Wiki, Marino, Rivers, Subritzky/Pirihiki, Witanga, Murupaenga and Solomon successions and four whānau trusts
summary: Form M.A. 835 (12254), Parengarenga 3G, 1264:3:00 (511.8261 ha), 55.000 shares. Pages 1–2: 'Compiled List of Owners as at 7.9.59', 57 owners (the share typed on the line above its owner on p.1) from Te Ahuru Rapihana Waaka .304 to Tiatoa Anaru .234 — Akinihi Wiremu 9.217 the largest; re-aligned the list sums exactly to 55.000. Pages 2–19, orders: Pita Anaru/Michael Andrews (1965); Ani Rata Taka → Rata Stanaway (1969); Ani Natanahira → Annie Murupaenga (1969); Emere Moihi → Marara Tilby (1970); Hami Rapihana Waaka → six Walker/Harrison/Pikaahu (1970); Ewhi Rauna Rapana → William Jordan Herewini (1970); Erana Umuroa Raharuhi → Clarence Umuroa (1972); AKINIHI HAURI ROHA (list 3, 2.292) → Raiha Wiripo Hone Kaihe solely (8.11.72); Eparaima Hori Reewe → Public Trustee → Katie Kerewai Paeahi Wanakore (1973–75); Pauhau Rupapera → Ngaroma Rupapera (1974); Atarangi Kaka or Arthur Wiki → eight Wiki (1975); Aue Umuroa Raharuhi → Herangi Matiu (Mrs R Matiu), Lena Ryder and six Fletcher (1976); Emere Wi Tamihana or Emere Ruka → fifteen Pirihiki/Subritzky, Matenga and Karena (1976); Eru Eru → ten Rivers (1977); Anamaraea Tamati → seven Marino (1973); Ani Henare → Henare Henare (1978); Akinihi Utika/Akinihi Wiremu (11.059) → three Hakaraia/Umuroa and the ten Rivers (1979); Hakiaha Tipene (1979); Apikaira Pene Aperahama → two Waata (1979); Apikera Haimona Riapo Puhipi → five (1981); Hohepa Anaru or Joseph Anderson → Public Trustee → eleven Anderson (1983); Aperahama Witanga → ten (1983); Reweti Wiki → Hohepa Rewiti Wiki (1987); Ani Murupaenga Rewiri → twenty-one (1987); Heni Wiki → Te Ranga Ngaro (1987); Manga Wiki → Martha Elizabeth McNaughton (1987); Karena Wiki → six Karena (1988); Arapani Witana Natanahira → six (1988); Anarua Karena → Waoroa Anarua Karena for life, remainder to seven incl. Pihopa and Tautoko Awarua Karena and 'Mei Matiu' (1989); Waimarama Karena → two (1989); Johnnie Marino → nineteen (1989); Witana or Nutana Wiki → twelve incl. 'Anokura Matiu' (1987); Henare Henare → eleven (1990; numbered 239, 340–349); Rita Marino → Tamati Howard as executor (1986); Mere Puru → four Ingley (1993); Hohepa Rewiti Wiki → ten (1996); RAIHA WIRIPO HONE KAIHE (Mrs George Solomon) or Raiha Wiripo Kaihe or Raiha Wiri Kaihe (list 70, 2.292) → six Solomon at 1/8 (incl. Wiripo William Solomon), two at 1/16 and seven Neho at 1/56 (1.2.96); Margaret Harrison → whānau trust (1997); Henare Hare Huru → Henare Harehuru & Makere Tibble Whānau Trust (1997); Hira Moihi or Cyril Hira Moses → four (1997); Paea Roberts → Motu and Paea Rapata Hoterene Whānau Trust (1995). Every order reconciles with the entry it replaces (the Murupaenga order by .001).

notes: CHECKED FOR WHĀNAU NAMES 23 Oct 2026. No tupuna of the Arama, Taniora Rihari, Hongi, Tangata, Matiu Wiripo, Paraihe or Te Patara lines is on the title. One lead — D022: 'Raiha WIRIPO Hone Kaihe (Mrs George Solomon) or Raiha Wiripo Kaihe or Raiha Wiri Kaihe', sole successor in 1972 to Akinihi Hauri Roha (presumably her mother), whose 1996 heirs include a son named Wiripo William Solomon. Wiripo is the name of Matiu Wiripo's father (T015) and of his brother Pirini Wiripo (T046) and of Pene Wiripo of Whakakoro (d. 1943); Rihari Matiu (T009) held Parengarenga B3A — so the Matiu Wiripo whānau had a Parengarenga foothold; which Wiripo was Raiha's father is untested. Other unplaced Matiu: Herangi Matiu (Mrs R Matiu) — the 'Herangi Fletcher or Mrs R Matiu' of Whatuwiwi 5 and 6, a daughter of Aue Umuroa Raharuhi; Anokura Matiu (1987); 'Mei Matiu' as a remainderman in 1989 (the Karikari Mei Raniera Matiu had died by 1985).

title: Takou Block — ownership schedule under the amalgamation order of 4 May 1991 (323.9320 ha; 665,000 shares): 420 owners, with the schedule of ownership orders nos 421–516, July 1991 – June 1998 (22 pages)
summary: Pages 1–10: the typed owners list attached to the Takou Block amalgamation order of 04/05/91 (LAND Takou Block; AREA 323.9320 ha; TOTAL SHARE 665000.000), 420 owners in alphabetical order of first name with sex/age and relative interest, hand-annotated with strike-throughs and the numbers of the later entries that replaced them; file no. 14236. Pages 11–22: the handwritten M.A. 835 'Schedule of ownership orders', entries 421–516 (10 Jul 1991 – 15 Jun 1998) — successions, vestings, gifts and whānau-trust orders citing Whangarei (WH), Kaikohe (KH), Aotea (AT), Rotorua, Ōtorohanga and Whakatāne minute books. Largest interests: Horitina Hori Tareha 24,623; Te Hira Mou Wiremu 22,150; Wi Parihi Mou Wiremu 21,716; Aperere Watene / Alfred Williams 18,937; Himi (Kutu) Hone Puru 17,771; Haare Puru 17,769; Ronald Taylor Hou 17,346; Edna Mary Paul 14,518 (life); Ngapine Reihana 12,901; Ngapine Haki 12,590; Hokena Wi Haare 12,027. Family groups visible from equal interests: Rihari (Hamuhamu Te Kiri, Ramiri, Tokowha, Whaekaimau 1,480.618 each; Sophie Robina, Taku, Ture, Whakaropai 357.449 each; Te Atarangi 2,323.558; Hetana 2,410.947; Meeke 1,479.791; Rehi 531.281), Kanuta Paerau, Kaiawe Parangi, Heihei, Kira, Haare, Hikuwai, Moana Hira, Rameka, Tahere, Tuhi, Tihi, Napia (388.122 each), Henry, Moihi. Whānau-relevant names: Mihiarangi Hulena or Taniora (2,741.935) and Warren Taniora (3,789.575 — the same figure as Rebecca Schneider); the Henry family (Maryanne 1,384.435 = Tania Dorretta Poulson; Teresa 2,675.389; Micheal John, Paul Stuart, Steven Richard, Wayne Andrew c. 374–378) — cf. Hoana Hetaraka Taniora 'or Hoana Henry' (T097); Ngawai Amato Riwhi Moihi 914.435 and Reupena Huperio Riwhi Moihi 4,595.820 — the Moihi/Amato whānau also on Tauaki (Arama Moihi alias Amato Riwhi Moihi, d. before 1917) and Taupo (Huperio Moihi, 1913; Taiapo Arama and Hapeta Arama Amato, Taupo No. 11); Paora Pita Taiapo and Manawhakaora Taiapo (Paora) — cf. the Taiapo Pita / Wirihana Taiapo owners of Te Wainui 2G; the Napia family (cf. Hare Napia, Otangaroa 1875); Taku Rihari and Aperahama Kaiawe Parangi, also owners of Waimate North; and the Kira, Wati Haare, Tame Hikuwai, Heihei and Taumaunu owners shared with Wainui A (1958) and Matauri X (1970). Arithmetic note: the 420 typed interests as read sum to 662,000.000 against the stated 665,000.000; the 3,000-share gap has not been located (either one thousands digit misread, or a typing error in the schedule).

title: Matangirau — hand-written list of owners by family group, with hapū (c. 1890s–1900s; ~90 names, part of a longer list numbered to 93)
summary: Three hand-written pages (no form): page 1 headed "Hiria Pa Matangirau …" lists owners with ages and a hapū column — the Tangiwai, Wirihana, Tame Te Awa, Rewi Paapu, Puatau, Haki Waata, Manahara Pona and Taniwha families; pages 2–3 (numbered 45–93) give the Paoro Hori, Nako Tauranga, Wiremu Ihaia, Hare Wiremu Ihaia, Honetua, Keepa, Himiona Maaka, Paerata and Taniwha families. The same Whangaroa whānau appear on the Wainui and Matauri records (Wiremu Ihaia, Kepa Tupe, Manahara, Himiona Maaka).

summary: Thirteen pages of Form 16 succession and vesting schedules for Wainui D (the parent of the 1958 Wainui A–C titles): Eme Patuhu's estate divided among c. 36 descendants of the 1890s owners (c. 1912–20); Mate Nako (1922); Hiria Haare (1925); the 29 Feb 1932 sitting (N66A — the same sitting that settled Taniora Rihari's estate at N66A/99–100): Wiremu Haare / Wi Haare (d. 1922) → Rena and Hokena Wiremu Hare 1/3 each and the four Moana Hira children 1/12 each; Haki Wiremu → Kiripata Heta Himiona; Hare Kepa Tupe → the Witeri Haora children; Hona Wiremu (d. 1919) → fourteen incl. title: Kaingapipiwai No 2 North A — succession schedules 1918–1932 (3 pages): Wini Moha, Ngawhare Rameka, Karena Hemi, Peti Toru, Tei Hepehi, and the 29 Feb 1932 sitting — TANIORA RIHARI (N66A/99) to 29 successors including Wiremu Arama Taniora (1/56)
court: Native Land Court, Tokerau (29 Feb 1932 sitting, N66A)
summary: Three schedule pages for Kaingapipiwai No 2 North A. Page 1 (1918–20): Wini Moha (15.11.16), 8.3.18 → the fourteen successors listed on 2 North B; Ngawhare Rameka (12.12.08), 5.3.19 → Maata Harete, Tauroa Himiona, Heki Taniora, Hapaira Maungu (f14), equally; Hau Eru alias Hau Eru Patuone (12.4.18), 1.3.19 → Ngawai Matarae, Hera te Kooti; Hemaima Pihema (24.4.18), 5.3.20 → Hana Tei solely; Marara Hone Pihema (1912), 5.3.20 → Meri Peita f17 solely. Page 2 (1923–32): Karena Hemi (10.4.17), 9.3.23 → Rina and Hoera Karena; Peti Toru (1920), 30.5.27 → seven Toru/Iraia/Ripeka children; Tauke Tango alias Tauke Tame (6.10.25), 6.5.29 → Hukatai Tame; Tei Hepehi (1918), 7.5.29 → six; Wikitoria Mangu (N66A/101, 1903), Katerina Ropiha (N66A/103, 1922), Te Whero Keina (N66A/103, 1921), all 29.2.32. Page 3 (typed, 29.2.32): TANIORA RIHARI, N66A/99, 1922 → Manga Taniora Rihari 1/7; Rihari 1/7; the seven Hetaraka Taniora children 1/49 each (trustee Rahera Hetaraka Taniora); the eight Arama Taniora children 1/56 each (trustee Peti Wiremu Tangata), among them WIREMU; the Pereene Kini, Tarapatiki, Ngarangi, Heremaia Kingi and Hamuera Herewini grandchildren (trustee Peti Kingi); then Haumia Rewi (N66A/106, 1916) → Rewi Paahu(?) solely. SIGNIFICANCE: Taniora Rihari held Kaingapipiwai 2 North A as well as Taupo 23C, and his succession here was made on the same day with the same 29 successors; Wiremu Arama's 1/56 of this interest is NOT among the five interests vested in Betty Hori in 1981 — a further interest of his estate whose present title status needs checking (the block does not appear by that name in the 2017 index).

title: Kaingapipiwai 1H — schedule of ownership orders: compiled list of 159 owners as at 26 Feb 1962 (35.000 shares; title s 70 Maori Vested Lands Administration Act 1954, 18 Sep 1958) with two 1963 orders; marked 'Sold to the Crown' (4 pages)
summary: Form M.A. 835 'Schedule of ownership orders' for KAINGAPIPIWAI 1H — title 'Sec 70 M.V.L. Act 1954 [Maori Vested Lands Administration Act] dated 18/9/58', area 202a 3r 14p, 35.000 shares — headed 'Compiled List of Owners as at 26/2/62', 159 owners in alphabetical order of first name (shares sum to 35.000), prepared/checked 22/6/62, followed by two 1963 orders: Puti Henare (or Riwhi, Rogers, Hemi) no. 109, .187, S.V.O. 11.3.63 (KT 1/97-98) → 160 Waiwhara Hensley or Rogers solely; Hiriwanu Tuta Rewha no. 36, .086, S.V.O. 26.6.63 (WH 35/203) → 161 Puke Rewha solely. Written diagonally across every page: 'Sold to the Crown' — the block has since passed out of Māori ownership, which is why no Kaingapipiwai 1H appears in the 2017 block index. Whānau-relevant owners: no. 102 'Peti Wiremu' .142 (probably Erihapeti/Peti Arama née Wiremu Tangata, d. 1960 — her mother Tura Wiremu was one of Hare Hongi Hika's successors on Kaingapipiwai No 1 in 1890); the other 1890 Hongi successors still on title — Moki Henare .429, Poni Rewharewha .429, Rati Poni .429; Wiremu Piri Hongi .007; the Hapeta Arama family (Mane, Mariana, Pouri, .125 each) and Taiapo Amato .375 of the Taupo No. 11 Arama Amato line; Tame Reweti 1.500 and Raiha Haki Reweti (Mrs Henare Paraone) 1.537 of the Reweti family that succeeded to 'Hariata Hongi' in 1894; large holders Hamiora Tuauru, Kepa Puru, Paora Heke and Wiremu Kowhai at 3.000 each, Hemi Tupe 2.000, Aperahama Parangi and Eruera Puke 1.000; the Flavell, Heke, Hape, Toetoe, Hapa, Nopera, Himiona, Tauroa and Haare Kainamu families.

title: Waikukupa — succession order lists 1880–1916 (typed list and three handwritten versions): Patara te Whakarorowai (1880) to Arama te Puhi and Horiana Motio; Rihari te Kuri (1894) to Taniora Rihari, Hemi Rihari and Matire Putete; Raiha Taniora (d. 24 Mar 1897) to her seven children, Taniora Rihari trustee (16 Jul 1898); Arama Patara alias Arama te Puhi (letters of administration 1898); Horiana Motio (1916) — 9 pages
summary: Nine pages of 'Waikukupa Block — Deceased / Date / Successors' lists: a typed fair copy (pp.1–3), a handwritten 'List of Succession Orders' with the deaths bracketed under the names (pp.4–6), an earlier struck-through handwritten list (pp.7–8) and a continuation sheet (p.9). ORDERS: Patara te Whakarorowai, 2.4.80 → Arama te Puhi m 1/2, Horiana Motio f 1/2 (p.7 dates it 9.10.96). Tana Toro, 5.5.82 → Panapa Kira. Hohepa te Taha, 25.6.91 → Makareta Turikataka f. Mohi te Pahii alias Mohi Nohinohi, 25.8.92 → Riwhi Moihi, Hapaira Kata, Mere Riwhi 1/3 each. RIHARI TE KURI (d. 15-10-85 or 86), 19.2.94 → Taniora Rihari m.a., Hemi Rihari m.a., Matire Putete f.a., 1/3 each. Mohi te Rahiri (d. 24-6-94), 24.10.94 → Tame, Piri and Hone Ruu (one share jointly), Horiona Motio one share. Riwhi te Pahi alias Riwhi Paru (d. 20-12-92), 24.10.94 → Hemi, Mere, Harata, Kuku and Wairama Riwhi equally. Hone Pihema alias Hone Pihama More, 24.10.94 → Maraea More, Hana Pei, Hariata Tauroa, Hera Waikere, Poni, Kaa, Meri and Marara Hone Pihema, 1/8 each. Pumipi alias Whaitua (d. 21-12-80), 25.5.97 → Kainamu, Te Rahui, Mere, Harata, 1/4 each. Hetaraka Arama (d. 20-9-80), 16.7.98 → Hone Tiaki. RAIHA TANIORA (d. 24-3-97), 16.7.98 → Hoana Pereme f.a., Himi Taniora m.a., Hetaraka Taniora m.a., Arama Taniora m.a., Rihari Taniora m.a., Manga Taniora m. 6 years, Matire Taniora f. 4, equally (1/7 each) — 'Taniora Rihari, Trustee for minors'; a marginal note 'sold 24-5-9?' stands against six of the seven. Panapa Kira (d. 20-12-89), 18.7.98 → Ngawati Panapa 1/3, Maraea Panapa alias Iwingaro 1/3, Mina Hami 1/6, Nehe Hami 1/6. Arthur Spickman, 10.11.98 → Peti Henare Kingi, Hemi Riiwhi, Poni Rewharewha, Tame Ru, Hone Arama, Maraea More (and Hone Ru on p.8), equally. Mere Hone Pihema, 14.11.98 → Maraea Mere, Hana Tei, Hariata Tauroa, Hera Waikere, Poni, Kaa and Marara Hone Pihema, equally. ARAMA PATARA ALIAS ARAMA TE PUHI (1 1/2 sh., No 1 and No 3A), 10.11.98 — Letters of Administration to Peti Henare Kingi and Poni Rewharewha; 'the devisees are (as to Waikukupa) Hone Arama [1 sh], Erana Arama [1/2], Matarai Arama [1/2], Peti Henare Kingi [1/2]' (three of the four marked sold). Hera Waikere (d. 19-9-00; share 30 3/4 acres), 26.11.01 → Repoama (12), Pati (10), Te Maunga (8) and Te Marepouri/Wharepouri Keri (6), 1 acre each, Pera Heta f 26 3/4 acres; Hana Tei trustee for the minors. WAIKUKUPA A (partition order 1901): Horiana Motio (N 56/311; d. 1915), 16.3.16 → Poni Rewharewha 1/7, Hira Hi Taniora 1/28, Hemo Hoera 1/28, Pinikera Hoera 1/28, Henare Tutere (9) 1/28, Wereta Hura 1/7, Kate Hemi 1/14, Puti Hemi 1/14, Pahi Puru 1/14, Ruakino Puru 1/14, Hau Toetoe 1/7, Rutete Toetoe 1/7.

notes: Whānau-relevant entries: (1) Rihari te Kuri → Taniora Rihari, Hemi Rihari, Matire Putete (the certificate is doc 1428614) — Taniora Rihari's father and siblings. (2) Raiha Taniora, wife of Taniora Rihari, died 24 March 1897; her seven children are named with the two youngest minors and their father as trustee — the earliest full list of that family, thirty-four years before the Taupo 23C succession of 1932 (doc 1527268). Her death in 1897 rules out the 'Rihipeti Arama' of Te Kohanga No. 1 who died in 1922 (D015). (3) Patara te Whakarorowai → Arama te Puhi and Horiana Motio: Arama te Puhi is Arama Te Patara (T148), Raiha's father, who also appears as 'Arama Whakapeka alias Arama Patara' (d. 17 May 1895) on Mangaiti No 1 — both estates passing to Peti Henare Kingi. (4) Poni Rewharewha, one of Hare Hongi Hika's seven successors of 1890 (Waihapa, Otangaroa, Kaingapipiwai), administered Arama Patara's estate and took 1/7 of Horiana Motio. The Waikukupa parent block is not in the 2017 block index; the record is pinned to its surviving subdivisions (C No 1, C No 2, G, D1, D2, H No 2).

title: Waikukupa — certificate of succession to Rihari te Kuri (d. 15 Oct 1885 or 1886): Taniora Rihari, Himi Rihari and Matire Ritete in equal shares, Whangaroa, 19 Feb 1894
court: Native Land Court, sitting at Whangaroa
judge: James Stephenson Clendon, Esquire, Recorder; Rehe Aperahama, Assessor
summary: Printed form N.L.C.-15 under the Native Land Court Act 1886 (Rule 28, Certificate of Succession to Realty). In the matter of the land known as Waikukupa, situate near Whangaroa, and of the estate, share or interest of Rihari te Kuri, deceased, therein. At a sitting of the Court held at Whangaroa before James Stephenson Clendon, Esquire, Recorder ("Judge" struck out), and Rehe Aperahama, Assessor: it is certified that Taniora Rihari m.a., Himi Rihari m.a. and Matire Ritete f.a., aboriginal natives, are the persons entitled to succeed "in equal shares" to the deceased's interest, and that the deceased died on the 15th day of October one thousand eight hundred and eighty-five "or eighty-six". Witness the hand of the Recorder and the seal of the Court this 19th day of February 1894. Margin: fees charged — witness 2/-, order 5/-.

summary: Twelve pages of the Ngatikahu memorial schedule (form M.A. 835), schedule pages 3 to 14; block area 1078.6894 ha, 75536.000 shares. Pages 3–9 are handwritten orders from 1973 to 1996: Pereene Eriha Kiwini or Greaves (45.492) → Mary Greaves as administratrix, 17.3.73; Ngareta Paul (14245.492) → Hemi or James Paul 25.492 and herself 14220.000 (4.11.75), then → Pimpi Paul 50.000 (23.3.77), then her estate → James (Hemi) Paul as administrator (17.12.81); Tamati Poharama (10000.000) → Toru Poharama 50.000 and himself 9950.000 (23.3.77), his estate → Te Paea or Sophie Poharama as administratrix (21.5.84) → twelve Poharama, Frasier, Haretiku, Bishop, Marsh and Heihei successors at 829.167 (30.10.88); Wiremu Topine → William Toloa Jnr → Simon Mathew Urlich (1978); Huruo Larkins → Glennis Pomare (1979); the estate of Polly Kingi or Ngahuia Kingi Waiaua (3147.050, N.Z. Guardian Trust administrator, 22.12.83) → Tauru, Ngatikahu, Erana and Wanahua Kingi Waiaua 1/7 each, John Henry Kingi and Marcia M Poharama 1/14, six at 1/42, and Kingi Reihana, Ketemaura Rutene, Oina Urlich Reihana and Eric Reihana 1/28; the Maori Trustee's 7194.292 shares → the Crown (s.153/53, 25.2.85); the Erana Kingi Waiaua (1984), Peremoana Rutene (1984), John Henry King (1985), Wiremu Rupapera (1988), Wanahua Kingi Simeon (1990), Eric Reihana (1991) and Eric Subritzky (1990) successions; the Hopa Ho Reihana Whanau Trust (11300.000, 21.9.94) and the Tauru Tuauru Henare Kingi Waiaua Whanau Trust (449.578, 19.7.96). Pages 10–14 are the typed list of 201 owners (nos 101–301, 7194.292 shares — the Crown's holding re-vested by order of 12.3.98, 85 WH 291-301) from Agnes Cochrane to Wirihana Motu, followed by no. 302 Ngatikahu Trustees, 21700.000 shares. On the typed pages the sex and share column was typed one line below its name; the values here are re-aligned and sum exactly to 7194.292.

notes: Checked for whānau connections 22 Oct 2026: no tupuna of the Arama, Taniora Rihari, Hongi, Wiremu Tangata, Matiu Wiripo, Paraihe or Te Patara lines appears on this block. The one exact name match — Wiremu Matiu (no. 299) — is the Karikari/Te Kohanga Wiremu Matiu, son of Matiu Paewoi (doc 1407032), not Matiu Wiripo's son (T141): he sits here with his siblings Raniera, Reihana, Miha and Tiini Matiu. Some forty of the 1998 owners (the Umuroa, Motu, Oti Rapihana, Iehu Timoti Puhipi, Haimona Riapo Puhipi, Rupapera, Raniera Matiu and Subritzky families) are also owners in Te Kohanga, Karikari 2 and Whakakoro F in the database — Ngatikahu belongs to the same Ngāti Kahu / Te Rarawa ownership community as those blocks. Lead: the rare name 'Pereene' (Pereene Eriha Kiwini or Greaves, list 19, d. before 1973) is the name carried by Werahiko and Te Uinga Pereene Kini, who took a quarter each of one seventh of Taniora Rihari's lands in 1932 — see D021 (Hoana Pereme, Raiha Taniora's eldest daughter in 1898, as the head of that line). Ngatikahu (block 30426, Taipa) is in the 2017 index.

summary: Pages 1–2: typed 'Compiled List of Owners as at 6.11.62' for Whatuwiwi 2B1, 316.667 shares — a faint carbon copy on which the first eighteen names (Bibi Kanara to Maki Kahiti Hapakuku or Mrs Woodcock) can be read but the share column cannot be matched reliably; superseded by the 1989 list (doc 1273091). title: Rangihamama X3A and Omapere Taraire E (aggregation of 6 May 1987) — list of about 2,015 owners as at 11 Mar 1992 (2,253,000 shares, 1997.56 ha), with the schedule page of 1992 orders (38 pages)
summary: Thirty-seven typed pages, 'List of Owners as at 11 March 1992' — Land: Rangihamama X3A and Omapere Taraire E; Title: Aggregation dated 6 May 1987; total area 575.2947 ha and 1422.2624 ha (1997.5571 ha); total shares 2,253,000.000 — about 2,015 owners in alphabetical order with list number, name, sex (where given) and shares, from 1 Aata Matini (404.869) to the Wiremu/Wiri entries of p.37; stamped 0003L 26.10.1992. The share column is typed one line below its name on every page (each page ends with a lone figure). Annotations strike through owners whose interests passed by later orders (e.g. Ururoa Hare Kainamu → 2546; Waata Paraihe or Walter Price → 2477–2482; Maehe Kire Tahere → whānau trust 2614; Section 86/93 5KH(S)114-116 of 30.03.2005 against Mackie Witute). Large holdings: Eri Wihongi 13,425.328; Hemi Pere Hetaraka and the Putahi Mountain reserve trustees (1190.769–1190.783 each); Uia te Maunga 3033.719; Te Wahukuri Tunga 3922.825; Heni Hohepa Heperi 3381.063; Reri/Meri Takiwira 3380.266; Rose Thompson and Maisey Reo (Mate) Heta Erueti 2892.170; Tupinia Tepara Burrows Puriri as executor for Margaret Josephine Puriri 4412.612. Page 38 (M.A. 835, the aggregation order's schedule): the Public Trustee of Napier as administrator of Ropati Hare Katene or Robert Charles Cotton (list 1375, 1196.896), s.81A/67, 24.8.92 → seven Cotton/Baker/O'Toole/Boynton successors at 170.985; Erana Kafere Mengia or Erana Radovanovich (list 215, 66.157), s.81/67, 21.9.92 → four executors.

notes: READ FOR WHĀNAU NAMES 23 Oct 2026. The list was machine-read (two scans, docs 1444625 and 1448800, merged): about 1,750 of the 2,015 names are recorded here from OCR and marked as such — their spelling and shares should be checked against the page before being relied on; the names of interest were verified by eye. No tupuna of the Arama, Taniora Rihari, Hongi, Tangata, Matiu Wiripo, Paraihe (Whangape) or Te Patara lines is on the title, but four name-echoes are logged as D023: the Paraihe = Price family (Albert Edward Price or Arapeta Paraihe and his brothers), the Cassidy whānau (cf. Makura Albert Cassidy Arama), William/James/Valencia Rangi Adams, and Te Paea Wereta Arama. Rangihamama X3A is not in the 2017 block index; the record is pinned to Omapere Taraire E and Rangihamama X3B.
